name: TokenHarbor
notes: Reseller with a pay-as-you-go wallet plus optional Passes (Agent, Office and Frontier, each a 7-day allowance), all behind one API key. It is modelled as pay-as-you-go: Cost is the list price from GET /v1/models (USD per million tokens, retrieved 2026-11-26), Pass discounts are not reflected, and there are no Quota Meters because TokenHarbor has no quota API. Terms: §3 "Proxy Reselling" forbids building "a direct, white-labeled proxy alternative to Token Harbor" without enterprise authorization. It is not flagged Terms Risk, because the operator uses their own key through external tools, which TokenHarbor allows (§2.1 mentions downstream end-users of your applications). A Provider Account on a Pass without wallet balance gets HTTP 402 model_not_in_plan for models outside its Pass: the 402 falls back to the next Provider Account without a Cooldown, and routing skips a Provider Account for models outside its Plan's coverage unless it is set to pay beyond its Plan. The model_not_in_plan code is observed live, not documented. A 429 (with Retry-After, or spend_limit_exceeded for a per-key cap set in the TokenHarbor dashboard) stays a Cooldown; the error for an empty wallet is undocumented, so there are no exhaustedErrorCodes. TokenHarbor serves every model on three chat endpoints, all checked live with bearer auth: chat completions, Anthropic Messages and Responses. Claude models list Anthropic Messages first and GPT models list Responses first (ADR 0095); the others use chat completions. Cached tokens are reported on chat completions (prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens) and on Anthropic Messages (cache_read_input_tokens). Where TokenHarbor publishes no cache read or cache write price, the price is left empty, as for the other resellers in the Catalog. The DeepSeek V4 Pro, V4 Flash, V4.1 Flash and V4.1 Flash 1017 models have lower prices in the TokenHarbor Off-Peak window (14:00-00:00 UTC every day). Long-context prices of the GPT-6 family and Claude Haiku 5.5 are in each model's notes only, so Cost understates very long prompts. Release dates are the day each model was first released by any Provider, copied from the original Provider's Catalog file or from models.dev; a -fast or -ultrafast variant takes its base model's release date and capabilities. Not shipped: the four :free models (TokenHarbor rotates its free list), and image generation, since /v1/images/generations has no Protocol here.
